exposure: Planned mode of delivery (vaginal vs. cesarean)
outcome: Neonatal outcomes (neonatal resuscitation requirements, Apgar scores at five minutes)
cohort: 275 women with a body mass index ≥50 who gave birth to a singleton pregnancy at ≥36 weeks gestation over a 10 year period at a single center in Melbourne, Australia
finding: Planned vaginal birth in women with super obesity was associated with lower rates of postpartum complications requiring readmission and similar neonatal outcomes compared to planned cesarean birth.
mod_finding: Multiparity was the strongest predictor of successful vaginal birth, while medical intervention in labor was associated with a reduced rate of success in primiparous women.
